title: 别把“洞察人心”玩成了“自我审视”

timeline.summary: A viewer asks how to stay indifferent while caring intensely about what others think.
Mikey says sensitivity and reading others are not inherently bad, but links anxious monitoring to approaching someone as lower status.
He contrasts this with a boss observing employees from a higher-status posture and calls that state attractive.
He repeats that monitoring someone framed as higher status creates a feeling of being scrutinized.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He distinguishes sensitivity itself from the posture used when interpreting other people.
claims.conditions: This is his status-based framing, not a clinical model.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He says observing others from a self-assigned higher-status role can look attractive, while monitoring someone treated as superior produces self-scrutiny.
claims.conditions: Hierarchy is contextual and subjective; do not use this to demean employees or suppress appropriate feedback.
